background: Indiana-rooted lifer who went from an Indiana Pacers intern/video and scouting role to a 17-year NBA assistant career: Sacramento (2009-13), Toronto under Dwane Casey (2013-16), Denver (2016-18, where he bonded with Chris Finch), Detroit under Casey (2018-21) and Minnesota as Finch's lead assistant (2021-26). In Minnesota he helped install Finch's read-based 'free-flow' offense, served as Finch's bench voice/acting coach during the 2024 playoff run after Finch's knee injury, and became a cult figure for his comic sideline-interview analogies ('the real-life Ted Lasso'). Hired by Portland on June 23, 2026 (introduced June 26) on a one-year guaranteed deal with two option years, over finalists Tyler Lashbrook and Tiago Splitter. Inherits a 42-40 playoff roster reshaped by Damian Lillard's return and a Ja Morant trade, plus Jrue Holiday, Scoot Henderson, All-Star Deni Avdija, Toumani Camara, Donovan Clingan and Yang Hansen. Stated identity: fast 'concept basketball' flow offense with multiple ballhandlers, heavy defensive pressure with a 'high line of scrimmage', a 10-man rotation, and 'play hard, smart and together for 48-plus.'

key_criticisms: No head-coaching experience; one-year guaranteed contract reflects uncertainty from the front office.
Must manage an overloaded, aging guard room (Lillard, Morant, Holiday, Henderson, Sharpe) with limited roles for young players.
Inherits the league's worst turnover team (17.3/game in 2025-26) while promising to push pace even harder.
Minnesota's offense under Finch/Nori was criticized for late-game stagnation in the 2024 and 2025 West finals (prior knowledge).
key_strengths: Elite communicator and culture-setter; helped build Minnesota's read-based flow offense (2021-26).
Clear modern identity: pace, ball movement, multiple handlers, pressure defense with a high pickup point.
Analytics-friendly, trend-aware (per Casey); plans a 10-man rotation that suits Portland's depth.
Steady under pressure as Finch's acting bench coach in the 2024 playoffs (Game 7 win in Denver).
